cases.explain: The suitcase is the subject of the question «где …?», so it stands in the plain dictionary form — the nominative.

cases.sentence: Я забегал по всему вагону в поисках ___.
cases.translation: I started running up and down the whole carriage in search of the little suitcase.
cases.explain: The phrase «в поисках» (in search of) governs the genitive, so чемоданчик becomes чемоданчика.

cases.translation: A person must give himself to other people.
cases.explain: «Отдавать» takes the recipient in the dative — the ones given to — so люди becomes людям.

cases.sentence: Он должен найти ___ и сказать им.
cases.translation: He must find people and say to them.
cases.explain: «Найти» takes a direct object in the accusative, and because люди is animate its accusative copies the genitive form людей.

cases.sentence: На запотевшем ___ чьим-то пальцем было написано.
cases.translation: On the misted-up window pane something had been written with somebody's finger.
cases.explain: «На» answering «где?» (a location, not a direction) requires the prepositional: на стекле.

cases.translation: One can't spend a whole lifetime tormenting oneself over this riddle!
cases.explain: The verb «терзаться» names the thing you torment yourself with in the instrumental; загадкою is the older, bookish variant of загадкой.

cases.sentence: Я схватился за ___ и вернулся в вагон.
cases.translation: I clutched my head and went back into the carriage.
cases.explain: «Схватиться за» (to grab hold of) takes the accusative of the thing seized: за голову.

reading.question: What does Venichka do right after the man who dragged him out dissolves into thin air?
options: He looks out of the window
reading.correct: He looks out of the window
reading.explain: Left alone in the vestibule, he looks out and sees that the blackness outside is gone.

reading.question: According to Venichka, how many stops are left after Pokrov before Petushki?
reading.explain: Seeing the sign «Покров» he cheers himself up: three stops and then Petushki.

reading.ru: Но почему же они оказались справа по ходу поезда?..
reading.question: What detail about the lights of Pokrov suddenly terrifies Venichka?
options: That they were on the right-hand side of the moving train
That there were far too few of them
That they went out as he watched
That they were reflected in his suitcase
reading.correct: That they were on the right-hand side of the moving train
reading.explain: If Pokrov passed on the right, then the train must be going the other way, from Petushki to Moscow.

reading.question: Whom does Venichka curse the moment he works out which way the train may be going?
reading.explain: He blames the Sphinx, who had earlier tormented him with riddles, for the reversed journey.

reading.ru: Я поглядел налево: там так же красиво было написано «…».
reading.question: What does Venichka find when he runs out and checks both sides of the vestibule?
options: The same word is written on the glass on both sides
Only the right-hand pane has writing on it
Both panes have been wiped clean
The writing has changed into a different word
reading.correct: The same word is written on the glass on both sides
reading.explain: Looking right and then left, he sees the same word written just as neatly on each pane, so the test proves nothing.

reading.question: What does Venichka discover as he runs up and down the carriage?
reading.explain: The suitcase is nowhere to be found, neither on the left nor on the right.

reading.question: What does Venichka's inner voice tell him to settle first?
options: The thought, and only then the suitcase
The suitcase, and only then the thought
The question of where he will spend the night
reading.correct: The thought, and only then the suitcase
reading.explain: The voice insists that he first sharpen his thought about where he is going, and look for the suitcase afterwards.

reading.ru: И вот – я запрокинулся, допивая свой остаток.
reading.question: How does Venichka reward himself for being noble?
options: By drinking up what is left of his Kubanskaya
By giving away his last money
By writing on the misted window
reading.correct: By drinking up what is left of his Kubanskaya
reading.explain: He toasts his own nobility and finishes the remainder of the bottle.

reading.ru: «Человек не должен быть одинок» – таково мое мнение.
reading.question: What opinion does Venichka announce once the darkness inside him clears?
options: That a person must not be alone
That a person must never travel at night
That a person should trust no one
That a person should always keep his suitcase close
reading.correct: That a person must not be alone
reading.explain: He declares that a person must give himself to others, even if they do not want to take him.

reading.ru: В первом – не было никого, только брызгал дождь в открытые окна.
reading.question: What does Venichka find in the first carriage he walks through?
options: Nobody, only rain spraying in through the open windows
reading.correct: Nobody, only rain spraying in through the open windows
reading.explain: The first carriage is empty except for the rain coming in at the windows; the second is empty too.

reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: There was somebody in the third carriage
He falls asleep in the vestibule
He finds his suitcase under a seat
reading.correct: There was somebody in the third carriage
reading.explain: After two empty carriages the chapter breaks off on the discovery that someone is in the third.

highlight.question: Which sentence works out that the train must be going from Petushki back to Moscow?
sentences: Вот – я сейчас отъезжал от станции Покров.
Я видел надпись «Покров» и яркие огни.
Все это хорошо – и «Покров», и яркие огни.
Но почему же они оказались справа по ходу поезда?..
Я допускаю: мой рассудок в некотором затмении, но ведь я не мальчик, я же знаю: если станция Покров оказалась справа, значит – я еду из Петушков в Москву, а не из Москвы в Петушки!..
highlight.explain: The long fifth sentence draws the conclusion from Pokrov having passed on the right.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells Venichka to go back out into the vestibule and take a better look?
sentences: Я онемел и заметался по всему вагону, благо в нем уже не было ни души.
Может, просто ты немного перепутал: может, Покров был все-таки слева, а не справа?
Ты выйди, выйди опять в тамбур, посмотри получше, с какой стороны по ходу поезда на стекле написано „…“».
highlight.explain: The last sentence is the instruction to step out again and check which side the writing is on.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the test with the suitcase that would prove he is travelling the right way?
sentences: А ты вспомни, Веничка, весь путь от Москвы ты сидел слева по ходу поезда, и все черноусые, все митричи, все декабристы – все сидели слева по ходу поезда.
И значит, если ты едешь правильно, твой чемоданчик должен лежать слева по ходу поезда.
highlight.explain: The third sentence turns the memory of where everyone sat into a test: the suitcase should be lying on the left.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what Venichka found in the first carriage?
sentences: В первом – не было никого, только брызгал дождь в открытые окна.
Во втором – тоже никого; даже дождь не брызгал…
highlight.explain: The second sentence reports the empty first carriage with rain coming in through the open windows.
